summary: Settings page: replace hardcoded DEFAULT_TRADITIONS with DB-driven /api/corpus
description:
src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:8-18 hardcodes DEFAULT_TRADITIONS — a client-side constant of 9 traditions and ~25 texts. The save endpoint persists which traditions are blocked, but the *catalog* never touches the DB, so:
- Adding a tradition or text requires a code deploy.
- The UI can promise traditions the retriever can't actually search (drift).

Replace with a server endpoint that aggregates what's actually in the corpus and switch the page to fetch on mount.

Approach:
- New route GET /api/corpus, auth-required (requireUser).
- Query: SELECT DISTINCT tradition, text_name FROM chunks ORDER BY tradition, text_name. Aggregating from chunks (rather than separate traditions/texts tables) means the UI only shows what is actually searchable.
- Response shape: { traditions: { [name]: { texts: string[] } } }.
- Settings page: drop DEFAULT_TRADITIONS, fetch /api/corpus in useEffect, render whatever comes back. NO hardcoded fallback — empty/error state is rendered as-is so a missing pg_restore is loud, not silent (per user feedback).

Tests:
- /api/corpus: 401 unauthenticated, returns aggregated shape, empty result is empty (no fallback).

Out of scope:
- tokens.tradition color map stays hardcoded (orthogonal — UI styling, not corpus data).
- Showing chunk_count per text (could be useful later; not required now).

resolution.test_function: aggregates DISTINCT (tradition, text_name) chunk rows into the catalog shape
resolution.note: Aggregating from chunks (not separate traditions/texts tables) so the UI is constrained to what's actually retrievable. No fallback per user feedback — empty corpus must surface, not be masked.
